pencereler.5-12: onto the carriages, and one hundred one people were killed. It began with a single wheel. The wheels had
pencereler.12-20: a steel tyre cushioned by rubber. That design came from trams, not high-speed trains. A fatigue crack grew until the tyre broke
pencereler.20-30: free. It jammed into the points and derailed the train. German high-speed trains switched to solid steel wheels.

segmentler.metin: The ICE at Eschede derailed and crashed into a bridge.
It took only a fatigue crack in a steel wheel tyre.
So how could a fatigue crack in a steel wheel tyre do this?

The answer is fatigue fracture of a rubber-cushioned wheel's outer tyre, which then struck the points — and it is why resilient wheels were replaced with solid monobloc wheels on German high-speed trains.
